results.text: So for energy policy, hedging and so on, the situation on the market today, I would bet that majority of competitors have more or less followed that the way our strategy [ is public ]. [#608](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-608)
And I would bet that majority of smaller competitors have been able to block at least the prices for '26. [#609](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-609)
Perhaps not '27, but for '26. [#610](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-610)
I don't consider that we will have a new competitive advantage, thanks to the increase of the spot price within energy. [#611](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-611)
So I don't think that it will change significantly, the situation. [#612](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-612)
And by the way, we need to keep in mind that the total energy costs represent 6% to 7% of the P&L -- of the top line in the P&L. [#614](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-614)
So it's not so massive. [#615](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-615)
So we see some increase of the spot price. [#616](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-616)
Even if the spot price increase double, okay, it would be a saving of 5%, 6% in comparison to small customers. [#617](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-617)
And you know that we are not pricing aggressive on the market. [#618](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-618)
We win contracts, thanks to reliability and quality, never because we destroy the prices. [#619](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-619)
So I don't expect to benefit too much from the situation on energy regarding the competitive landscape. [#620](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-620)
Second question regarding the sequence of the organic growth and impact of the slowdown of signature at the end of the year. [#622](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-622)

So what is for me, quite interesting and quite promising for the midterm is the fact that we have registered some quite good signature in the beginning of the year '26, the first 2 months. [#623](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-623)

And when we will analyze the sequence of the organic growth of the group, what we expect because it is signed, not already put in place, and it is the installation of the contracts that will arrive around summer for some contracts. [#624](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-624)
And a super big contract in health care in Germany, we are talking about EUR 30 million per year. [#625](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-625)
That will start to be implemented in October, November. [#626](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-626)
So we are quite confident to see a sequence improving all over the year '26. [#627](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-627)
So probably a growth that will be better in H2 '23 than H1 of '26. [#628](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-628)
And not because we expect it is because it is signed, just timing to start to invoice. [#629](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-629)
Perfect. [#631](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-631)
Can I just ask a quick follow-up on the energy cost? [#632](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-632)
I think you guide to about EUR 190 million of gas and electricity cost in '26. [#633](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-633)
I think in '24, the number was about EUR 240 million. [#634](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-634)
Do you have the 2025 energy cost, excluding vehicle fuel, to hand? [#635](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-635)
Yes. [#637](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-637)

To be even more precise in terms of saving in euro, if you take the 2- to 3-year evolution, it's more or less -- in '24, we made a saving around EUR 40 million in comparison to '23. [#638](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-638)
In '25, it is a savings of around EUR 30 million. [#639](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-639)
We expect in '26, a saving around EUR 20 million. [#640](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-640)
And for now, what we see for '27 should represent another saving around EUR 10 million to EUR 15 million. [#641](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-641)
Your next question today comes from the line of Sabrina Blanc from Bernstein. [#643](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-643)

Could you come back for one -- my first question, could you come back on the financial cost for 2026 if we have to compare to 2025 and after taking into account, the refinancing mentioned by Louis? [#645](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-645)

And second question is regarding -- you have mentioned potentially some share buyback or special dividend in terms of capital allocation. [#646](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-646)
So could you come back on the -- what is your preference compared to the current market environment? [#647](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-647)
Regarding interest, your question is P&L or cash? [#649](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-649)
Both. [#651](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-651)
So P&L, we shall have another small increase in the same magnitude as '25 for the same reason. [#653](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-653)
And basically, the stable -- the debt is stable, but the new debt are slightly more expensive than the old debt. [#654](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-654)
For cash, it's less regular, and we shall have a strong decline of the cash interest. [#655](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-655)
So we paid like EUR 99 million this year, and it shall be EUR 10 million lower in '26. [#656](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-656)
And the majority is linked to the coupon we paid in '25, as you're aware. [#657](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-657)

Regarding your question on the last [ core ] of the capital allocation policy, you see what we do in '26, which is a part of the answer, all in buyback. [#659](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-659)
And the global answer, the generic answer is that it depends on the market condition, of course. [#660](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-660)
And of course, obviously, the stock price. [#661](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-661)
Your next question today comes from the line of Karl Green from RBC Capital Markets. [#663](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-663)
Just two outstanding questions from me. [#665](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-665)
Firstly, just on Pest Control, you talked about the 2.5% loss rate improvement. [#666](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-666)
How much further is there left to go in that area? [#667](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-667)
And also in terms of the like-for-like growth, how much of that was cross-selling versus kind of stand-alone Pest Control sales? [#668](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-668)
The second question, just slightly more technical around the share-based payments. [#670](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-670)
You mentioned that there was that change in increased employer contributions in terms of tax implications. [#671](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-671)
All other things being equal, are we likely to see a follow-through to fiscal '26? [#672](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-672)

Clearly, you can't predict the share price over the balance of the year, but would we expect that share-based payments charge to keep going up a little bit or stay broadly stable? [#673](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-673)
I will start with Pest Control. [#675](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-675)
So yes, the quality of the operation of Elis has allowed us to decrease the level of loss rate. [#676](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-676)

And we are quite super proud because even if we are still a small player in the world, I think that in terms of reliability and the quality of service delivered and efficiency of our interventions, we are at a super good level. [#677](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-677)
So we still have some margin to continue to decrease a little, the loss rate, probably not with the same magnitude of 2.9 points. [#678](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-678)
Nevertheless, when we see the breakdown by country and so on, we still have some region where we could be even more efficient. [#679](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-679)
So it will, I think, still continue to decrease a little. [#680](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-680)

Regarding the second part of your question, the origin of the growth, it is a good mix between cross-selling and pure [ virgin account ]. [#682](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-682)
You know and it is what we have explained in more and more countries now we operate through a specific business line. [#683](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-683)
So that means that for us, it's not really an issue to open some new accounts with Pest Control. [#684](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-684)

But it is -- at the end, it is a good mix between cross-selling with existing customers and opening of new accounts, thanks to Pest Control. [#685](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-685)
Regarding your technical question on IFRS 2 treatment. [#687](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-687)
So in the EUR 46 million you have in '25, 3 components. [#688](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-688)
First, the free shares program, EUR 26 million. [#689](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-689)

Second, the tax linked to this free share program of EUR 11 million, which encompass a bit of stock treatment, as all the stock has been impacted by the 30% new tax. [#690](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-690)

And there is a third component, which is EUR 9 million of kind of subsidy to the capital increase reserve to employees, which was a big success in '25. [#691](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-691)
So once I've said that, you understand that we have a couple of one-offs in '25. [#692](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-692)
So it shall be smaller in the future. [#693](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-693)
But the free share program accounting is linked to the stock price. [#694](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-694)
So there, I cannot say what it will be and when delivered. [#695](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-695)
But so all in, between EUR 40 million and EUR 45 million is a good idea to have in mind. [#696](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-696)
Your next question today comes from the line of Olivier Calvet from UBS. [#698](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-698)
Olivier Calvet covering for [ Louis Wizer ]. [#700](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-700)
I have two questions left. [#701](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-701)
First on volume and price. [#702](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-702)
What was the split of volume and price in the '25 organic growth? [#703](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-703)
And what do you expect for '26? [#704](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-704)
And then you gave some color on adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBIT. [#705](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-705)

I just wanted to know if you could discuss how you see the evolution of cost in '26 besides the energy and productivity topics on the labor, distribution costs, SG&A, perhaps? [#706](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-706)
Volume and price is more or less the same, I would say, in '25 and '26. [#708](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-708)
So it's a mix of volume and price, equally split, I would say, to roughly summarize. [#709](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-709)
So same volume growth and price growth in '25, and it's more or less what we expect also for '26. [#710](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-710)
The inflation of our cost is mainly due to wages. [#711](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-711)
We expect in '26, wages that will be around 4% increase at the group level. [#712](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-712)
Of course, less in some countries like France, much more in LatAm. [#713](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-713)
We discussed the situation in Colombia. [#714](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-714)
So for the rest, can you perhaps explain a little more, the second part of your question, please? [#715](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-715)
Yes, sure. [#717](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-717)
Just on the distribution costs and SG&A side of things, if you have specific expectations you'd like to break down? [#718](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-718)
No specific things to highlight. [#720](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-720)

Logistic cost, it is -- we have -- you know that we have developed some internal tool to optimize the route distribution at every laundry level. [#721](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-721)

So we are close to roll out now these new tools everywhere, and it is part of the productivity program that we have at the group level. [#722](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-722)
When I say that we expect 2% to 3% gains in every topic, logistics is one topic. [#723](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-723)
And so nothing special to highlight in light with what we have delivered in the past. [#724](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-724)
And SG&A, I have no specific subject to comment at this stage today. [#725](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-725)
Your next question today comes from the line of Oliver Davies from Rothschild & Co. [#727](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-727)
Two questions for me. [#729](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-729)
So just firstly, on the margin. [#730](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-730)

Obviously, LatAm was quite a big drag on group margins last year, but you said that you kind of expect that to be flat to up this year, along with some margin expansion in France. [#731](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-731)
So which regions do you expect margin expansion to be tougher this year, I guess, given the guide for a slight improvement overall? [#732](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-732)

And then secondly, just on the headline net income per share guide, how much of the buyback are you assuming is executed to get to that high single-digit number? [#733](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-733)
So yes, in France, we expect another small improvement of the margin like in LatAm. [#735](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-735)
Normally, we expect also probably margin improvement in Southern Europe. [#736](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-736)
In the other region of the group, so Central Europe, U.K., Ireland and Nordics, we will be probably more cautious. [#737](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-737)
In Nordics, you know that the margin is quite stable, so we don't expect any major move. [#738](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-738)
In Germany, we know that we have also a huge increase of the minimum wage that has been decided for the year '26. [#740](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-740)
And in a context where in health care, we have a lot of public contracts. [#741](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-741)
We have a kind of competition on price and so on. [#742](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-742)
So it will not be so easy to apply immediately, the price increase needed to offset this inflation of the wages due to minimum wage. [#743](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-743)
So I will be quite cautious with the expectation of margin in Germany, so that will affect Central Europe. [#744](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-744)
And in U.K., we have now reached quite a strong level of margin, above 32%. [#746](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-746)
If you remember, we started 7 years ago or 8 years ago at 23% only. [#747](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-747)
And so in that context, we are forced to be quite cautious with the expectation. [#748](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-748)

It is an area where we have a solid competitor with [ Johnson ], some other tough competitors on the market with the Scottish one, with [ Clean ] also. [#749](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-749)
So it's -- we need to be cautious now, reaching 32%. [#750](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-750)

I think that we have always said that in U.K., we will have sometimes some limits in the margin development due to the level of competition. [#751](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-751)
It's not the case in Southern Europe. [#752](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-752)
So it's the global picture that we have at this stage of the year regarding evolution of the margin, globally speaking for '26. [#753](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-753)
Your second question was on EPS development and the relationship with share buybacks. [#755](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-755)
Well, you would agree that high single digit is a kind of bracket. [#756](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-756)
We already did EUR 114 million of buyback up to now. [#757](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-757)
And it adds, of course, to what we did last year. [#758](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-758)
Technically -- I will answer technically. [#759](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-759)
You know that for this calculation, we take the average number of shares. [#760](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-760)
It means that the day you buy the share is very important in the calculation. [#761](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-761)

It means also that what you do at the beginning of the year has a massive impact versus what you do at the end of the year, which is more for next year actually in terms of impact. [#762](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-762)
So that's why -- I mean, if we do, I don't know, 400 or 600, the difference will be made at the end of the year. [#764](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-764)
It doesn't change a lot, the EPS growth for '26. [#765](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-765)
It changes, of course, for '27. [#766](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-766)
The second point, of course, is the price in the model is very -- is kind of important, which price you buy the shares. [#767](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-767)
[Operator Instructions] And your next question today comes from the line of Mourad Lahmidi from [ Elis ]. [#769](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-769)
I have two questions, please. [#771](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-771)
So the first one is on the convertible bond and the link to the share buyback. [#772](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-772)
So I didn't hear the strike price of the convertible bond. [#773](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-773)
So if you can just say it again, that would be kind. [#774](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-774)
And the second question, so the EUR 500 million share buyback, that's about 20 million shares at current share price. [#776](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-776)
How many shares do you expect to cancel versus use to cover the share-based payment program? [#777](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-777)
And the second question is on the churn. [#778](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-778)
Could you just comment on how this KPI has evolved across 2025? [#779](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-779)
And what do you see during the start of the current year? [#780](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-780)
I will start with the second part of the question and give the floor to Louis after. [#782](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-782)
No major change and stabilization of the performance regarding churn. [#783](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-783)
So it was quite stable at the end of the year '25 and no big change in '26, in the beginning of '26. [#784](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-784)
What I have highlighted in terms of change of trend is more for signature of new contracts. [#786](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-786)
So quite smooth end of Q3 and beginning of Q4 and better end of the year and strong beginning of new year. [#787](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-787)
So that's why probably less organic growth in H1 and more organic growth in H2, as I said. [#788](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-788)
So it is more with new signature that we have seen a small change in the level of performance and quite stable for the churn. [#789](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-789)
Technical question on the convertible, I mentioned the threshold at which we can force conversion. [#791](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-791)
The strike is 30% below that is EUR 16 after dividend payment in May. [#792](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-792)
So EUR 16, it means that you have like 23 million of shares linked to this bond. [#793](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-793)

If you make the calculation, if we do all the buyback before the redemption debt, it means that we will use all the buyback shares to reimburse the convertible at the end of the year. [#794](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-794)
That is on the -- I mean, alternatively, a part can be used also for the free share of the program, but it's quite minimal. [#795](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-795)
Sorry, just to confirm, you will cancel those shares? [#797](https://gam.prontonlp.com/#/ref/$SENTID_T000003676656-797)
